source_note: See data/wow_spells/README.md for the schema. Every entry's values are read live from its own WoW: Forever Wowhead spell tooltip (wowhead.com/forever/spell=<wowhead_spell_id>) unless "notes" says otherwise. This file is a schema-validation pass on a third class (Combat spec), not yet a complete glossary the way Warrior's is.
gaps: Only the Combat single-target rotation pieces are covered (Sinister Strike, Backstab, Eviscerate, Slice and Dice). Ambush (stealth opener), Instant Poison (weapon buff named in the real rotation), Gouge, Kick, Sprint, and all Assassination/Subtlety trees are not looked up.

French names for Backstab, Eviscerate and Slice and Dice were NOT found from a reliable source this pass (only Sinister Strike's real FR name, "Attaque pernicieuse", is confirmed, via data/wow_talents/rogue.json's own Improved Sinister Strike entry) -- left in English with a note rather than guessed.

Eviscerate's Attack-Power scaling coefficient: the tooltip states the ability's damage "increased by Attack Power" but the exact coefficient wasn't visible in the effect breakdown captured this pass (unlike e.g. Mage spells, which show an explicit "SP mod: X").
Combat's own Dual Wield Specialization (n105740, Combat tree) wasn't cross-checked against Warrior's for whether Rogue's version has the same real values -- don't assume they match.

Real, sourced finding (2026-09-25): Assassination and Subtlety's own level-20 guides describe the SAME sustained single-target core rotation as Combat -- build combo points with Backstab (behind target) or Sinister Strike, spend at 5 combo points on Eviscerate or Slice and Dice. Each spec's real differences are its talents (now catalogued below), a one-time stealth opener (Ambush, Subtlety/Assassination), and poisons (Instant Poison, all three specs -- still unsourced). None of those are modeled by this project's simulator yet, so all three specs currently produce the same simulated number: a real, disclosed limitation, not a mistake. Ghostly Strike (Subtlety's own granted ability, a non-positional Backstab alternative) is real but its own cost/cooldown/damage aren't sourced yet.

abilities.notes: Rank 3 is the max rank trainable by level 20 (Rank 4 requires level 22). Real finding validating the schema on this class: Rogue's own GCD is 1 second, not the 1.5 seconds already confirmed for Warrior and Mage -- the schema already supports this correctly (gcd_sec is per-ability, not a hardcoded constant), this is the first real confirmation it differs by class.

Rank 3 is exactly the level-20 cap. Real single-target priority (Icy Veins) uses this over Sinister Strike whenever positioned behind the target -- higher combo-point-per-Energy value (60 Energy/1 CP vs Sinister Strike's 45 Energy/1 CP) is offset by the higher direct damage, not by CP generation rate.

Rank 3 is the max rank trainable by level 20 (Rank 4 requires level 24). Real per-combo-point damage table from the tooltip, not derived: 1 CP 25-39, 2 CP 44-58, 3 CP 63-77, 4 CP 82-96, 5 CP 101-115 (a clean +19 per point pattern, but the table itself is the sourced value, not the pattern). Also scales with Attack Power per the tooltip's own text; exact coefficient not captured this pass (see gaps).

Rank 1 is the max rank trainable by level 20 (Rank 2 requires level 42). A flat +20% melee attack speed buff whose DURATION scales with combo points spent (a genuinely linear real formula, unlike Eviscerate's damage table): 1 CP=9s, 2 CP=12s, 3 CP=15s, 4 CP=18s, 5 CP=21s (base 6 + 3×CP). Per this schema's non-stacking rule, recasting while active replaces the remaining duration, it does not add to it.
